versicolor_corr = df.loc[df['species'] == 'Iris-versicolor', 'petal_length_cm'].corr(df.loc[df['species'] == 'Iris-versicolor', 'petal_width_cm'])

analysis = df.assign(missing_sex=df['sex'].isna())
result_species = analysis.groupby('species').agg(rows=('sex','size'),missing=('missing_sex','sum'),rate=('missing_sex','mean'))
result_island = analysis.groupby('island').agg(rows=('sex','size'),missing=('missing_sex','sum'),rate=('missing_sex','mean'))
result = {'by_species': result_species.to_dict(), 'by_island': result_island.to_dict()}

final_finding.title: Duplicates Concentrated in Quality Scores 5, 6, and 7
final_finding.summary: Exact duplicate rows are not uniformly distributed; they are concentrated in quality scores 5, 6, and 7, while scores 3 and 4 have no duplicates. This suggests a systematic pattern rather than random ingestion errors.
final_finding.recommended_action: Investigate the source data for quality scores 5, 6, and 7 to determine if duplicates are intentional (e.g., repeated measurements) or result from a systematic ingestion process.
